verdict.rationale: pnpm's docs say it is a drop-in npm replacement that works on existing projects with no migration. Its own conversion behavior is documented: `pnpm install` auto-creates `pnpm-workspace.yaml` from existing workspace patterns, and a `hoisted` nodeLinker mimics npm/Yarn Classic layouts. Community reports of successful yarn/Lerna/npm migrations corroborate this, though some needed `--shamefully-hoist`. missing for 10: documented lockfile import/conversion from npm or yarn lockfiles, a dedicated migration guide or command, documented handling of incumbent-specific config beyond workspace patterns.

support.subject: As a switcher, I can migrate an existing project from the incumbent tool with documented import or conversion tooling

citations.quote: pnpm is a drop-in replacement for npm. Point it at any existing project — no migration, no rewrites, no lockfile gymnastics.
When such a repository has no `pnpm-workspace.yaml`, `pnpm install` creates one with the same patterns and links the listed projects on that same install
set the nodeLinker setting to `hoisted`. This will instruct pnpm to create a node_modules directory that is similar to those created by npm and Yarn Classic.
I migrated a large project from yarn to pnpm and the speed difference is insane, both in local development and CI.
